title: Render per-range styled text in vector PDF export (emitType consumes CharacterRuns)
outcome: A document whose text story carries CharacterRun overrides exports to vector PDF with each span painted at its own size/fill/font (per-run Tf and color operators, per-range embedded faces when fontId overrides exist), glyph positions matching the canvas compose-for-compose, and the export report telling the truth about what was emitted.
before: Batch critic finding 2026-08-28 (post-merge review, local main 5014465+): since VIRO-0142, composeFrame positions glyphs at mixed-size per-run advances, but src/export/pdf.ts emitType still paints every glyph with the story-level size/fill and a single embedded face. Reproduction: two ranges (size 64 copper / size 34 blue) via type.characterRange -> canvas correct; exported PDF paints every glyph ~12pt black scattered across the wide advances (critic shots styledpdf-01-canvas.png vs styledpdf-03-crop.png); export report claims success with no caveat - a false success state. Severity P1: export accuracy is a core product promise; failure is silent; exposure currently bus/Anchor-only (no chrome authoring UI yet).
after: emitType segments stories by runs exactly as the engine does, emits per-span Tf/fill (and per-range faces when required), and the PDF render matches the canvas; if any range aspect remains unexportable, the report records it explicitly.
acceptance: A two-range document (different size + fill) exports to PDF whose pdf.js render shows both spans at their correct sizes/colors (rendered-pixel + text-content proof, artifact-level).
Glyph advance positions in the PDF match the canvas composition (no scatter).
Per-range fontId overrides either embed per-range faces or produce an explicit truthful report entry - never silent divergence.
VIRO-0015 corpus text pins updated to the new topology; all other pins unchanged; compound/font/effects suites stay green.
npx tsc --noEmit, corpus + new tests, npm run test:chrome and npm run build pass.
evidence: pdf.js rendered proof: both ranges correct size/color
Updated corpus text pins + green suites

builder.candidate: 2803570 (on b1ad608 emitType core + 199ef28 node suite; base fc96f44)
builder.approach: emitType segments composed glyphs exactly as the engine composed them: one styled run per distinct (face, size, fill); each run emits its own gs/Tf/rg inside the line's single BT/Tm/ET text object and writes its glyph ids ONLY under its own embedded face, resolved through faceFor (cached per FacePack id, so each face is embedded once). Word-space re-insertion now tests the pen gap against the smaller of the following run's space and the story-level space, so a boundary between differently sized runs still extracts a word break. composeFrame is called with layer.textFrame - the exact drawTypeFrame call - so PDF type placement honors 0143 insets/vertical alignment; the 0146 type-shadow silhouette uses the same args. A legacy faceFor fast path that could return the wrong face once a second face was embedded was removed. Report: textRuns is one per styled TJ run; multi-face embeds name every face and disclose the total full-font byte cost in report.notes.
builder.size_impact: Per-range faces embed whole (0145 policy). Measured: Noto Sans Regular 2001 KB + Noto Serif Regular 1163 KB = ~3.1 MB of font data in the two-face fixture; the report states the per-document face count, names and KB total in notes whenever more than one face is embedded. Single-face documents are unchanged from 0145.
builder.notes: No silent divergence path remains: same-face ranges share one font resource; cross-face ranges get one font resource per face; an unresolvable range fontId falls back to the story face exactly as the canvas does (fontRegistry.resolve contract in engine/type.ts), so PDF and canvas cannot disagree.
